sheet-194.description: Sheet 194 of the Paterson volume 2 series, a new sheet of April 1922 covering the southern end of the Borough of Hawthorne at 100 feet to an inch. It is bounded on the north by Diamond Bridge Avenue, on the east by Royal Avenue and the New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad, and runs south past Elberon Avenue to the edge marked no exposure. Lafayette Avenue crosses the sheet on a slant from Diamond Bridge Avenue to Lincoln at the bottom, with Grand Avenue parallel to it along the railroad. West of Lafayette a regular grid of 50 foot lots lines May and Hale and the cross streets Cedar, South, Llewellyn, Tuxedo, Maitland, Franklin and Elberon Avenues, almost all frame dwellings with private garages, and a few poultry houses. Two ponds lie in a large lot at the north-west corner. Along Lafayette Avenue and Diamond Bridge Avenue are stores, a public library at the corner of Grand Avenue, St. Clemen's Mission Episcopal Church and the First Reformed Church. The fire department's Hose Company No. 1 stands on Grand Avenue. South of Maitland Avenue, between Lafayette and the railroad, the Cylinder Manufacturing Company has lumber sheds, and a contractors' supply shed stands beside the tracks. Public School No. 5 is at the corner of May Street and Elberon Avenue. Six inch water pipes are drawn along most streets, with an eight inch main in Lafayette Avenue and a twelve inch main in Diamond Bridge Avenue. Names of the streets on sheet 200 are lettered across Diamond Bridge Avenue at the top.
notes: May and May (West) are both May Street today; the sheet draws them offset at Cedar Avenue.
Cedar Lane is Cedar Place today; Hale is not in OpenStreetMap.
Bromford Avenue at the top is printed Bamford Avenue on sheet 200 (Bamford Avenue today).
Copyright stamp dated Aug 28 1922 at the top.

map, 100 ft. Lafayette Av, May St (May (West) north of Cedar), Cedar, South, Llewellyn, Tuxedo, Maitland, Franklin, Elberon, Grand, Royal Avs, Diamond Bridge Av along the top; NYS&W RR on the east. Hale St and Cedar Lane not in OSM (Cedar Lane = Cedar Place). One part.

sheet-195.description: Sheet 195, a new sheet of April 1922 at 100 feet to an inch, covering the western side of Hawthorne north of Rea Avenue. Goffle Road runs diagonally down the west side of the sheet, and Goffle Brook (lettered Brook) winds south through the middle, widening into a pond above Rea Avenue where two concrete culverts carry the road over it; a feed mill and feed warehouse, an apartment house and an auto service station stand at the corner of Goffle Road and Rea Avenue. East of the brook is a regular grid of 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th Avenues and Lafayette Avenue running north and south, crossed by Van Winkle, Genevieve, Florence and Rea Avenues; Railroad Avenue enters at the right edge. Most blocks are laid out in narrow house lots, many still empty, with frame dwellings, garages, poultry houses and sheds scattered among them. Lafayette Avenue near Rea Avenue is the main commercial stretch, with stores, a barber, drug and hardware stores and the Fire Department No. 1 house with its equipment listed. The First Reformed Church of North Paterson stands on 3rd Avenue at Rea Avenue. Water pipes of four, six, eight and twelve inches are drawn in the streets. The large lot at the north-west, between Goffle Road and the brook, is blank. Sheet numbers of the adjoining sheets 196, 197 and 199 are printed at the edges, and Alexander and Hutchinson Avenues from sheet 197 are lettered at the top right.
notes: The brook is Goffle Brook; only 'Brook' is lettered.
Railroad Avenue is Utter Avenue today; Alexander Avenue is Alexandria Avenue and Hutchinson Avenue is Hutchison Avenue.
Copyright stamp dated Aug 28 1922.
map, 100 ft. Goffle Rd, Goffle Brook, 1st-4th Avs, Lafayette Av, Van Winkle, Genevieve, Florence, Rea Avs. One part.

sheet-197.description: Sheet 197, a new sheet of April 1922 drawn at a larger scale than its neighbours (a scale of feet that works out to 50 feet to an inch), covering the north-east corner of Hawthorne between Lafayette Avenue and Ethel Avenue, from Wagaraw Brook and Douglas at the top down to Van Winkle Avenue. Alexander, Hutchinson and Short run north and south across Roosevelt Avenue (Lee Avenue), and a trolley right of way cuts diagonally from Van Winkle Avenue towards the north-east, with Ethel Avenue parallel to it. Nearly the whole sheet is surveyed house lots, most of them empty; frame dwellings, coops, garages and an auto repair shop with a gasoline tank stand along Lafayette Avenue, and a carpet weaver's shop is noted there. Public School No. 6, a hollow tile and brick building with reinforced concrete floors in its corridors, stands on the block between Alexander and Hutchinson north of Roosevelt Avenue. Between the trolley right of way and Ethel Avenue the Arnold and Young Silk Company has its broad silk mill, with its watchman and power noted. Wagaraw Brook crosses the top of the sheet. Water pipes of six and twelve inches are drawn in the streets. Sheets 173, 195 and 199 adjoin at the edges.
notes: Alexander Avenue is Alexandria Avenue today, Hutchinson Avenue is Hutchison Avenue and Short is Short Street.
The trolley right of way is followed by today's 4th Avenue; it was not used as control because the modern line departs from the drawn one by 3 to 8 m.
Drawn at 50 feet to an inch although no scale note is printed; the fitted scale (7.81 px/ft) confirms it.
Copyright stamp dated Aug 28 1922.

map, 50 ft (Scale of Feet bar, no '100 ft' note); Lafayette, Alexander (now Alexandria Av), Hutchinson (now Hutchison Av), Short St, Roosevelt Av (Lee Av), Ethel Av, trolley right of way (now 4th Av, left out: modern line off the drawn one), Douglas Av and Wagaraw Brook at top. Van Winkle Av junctions hand-picked (south side not drawn). One part.

sheet-198.description: Sheet 198, an additional sheet of April 1922 at 100 feet to an inch, drawn turned on the page so that north points to the left. It covers the north-eastern grid of Hawthorne between Railroad Avenue on the left (north) and Central Avenue on the right (south), with the numbered avenues 5th to 11th running across the sheet and Rea, Ekings, South, Horton and Parker Avenues running down it. 11th Avenue is marked not open. The western blocks are almost entirely surveyed 25 foot lots with only a scattering of frame dwellings, coops, garages and a painting shop; the large blocks between Horton, Parker and Central Avenues hold a few more houses, an auto and plumber's shop and a concrete-block machine shop. Along Central Avenue a row of dwellings faces the adjoining sheet 201, with Park Ave and Forest Ave lettered where they leave to the right. Below 5th Avenue two large empty blocks run down to the New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad at the foot of the sheet, and a strip at the lower left belongs to sheet 196 and is only outlined, with a few buildings of the rail yard. Six and eight inch water pipes are drawn in the streets. The north arrow and scale are at the lower left, and the title and stamp at the top right.
notes: Railroad Avenue is Utter Avenue today.
South (between Ekings and Horton Avenues) is not in OpenStreetMap.
Turned sheet: north is to the left.
Copyright stamp dated Aug 28 1922.
map, 100 ft, turned: north to the left. Railroad Av (now Utter Av), Rea, Ekings, South, Horton, Parker, Central Avs, 5th-11th Avs, Park Ave, Forest Ave. One part.

sheet-199-1.description: The left part of sheet 199, an additional sheet of April 1922 at 100 feet to an inch, separated from the right part by a heavy line and drawn turned so that north points to the left. It covers the grid of Hawthorne between Van Winkle Avenue on the left and Railroad Avenue on the right, with Genevieve and Florence Avenues between them, crossed by the numbered avenues 9th, 8th, 7th, 6th and 5th, and further down by Ethel Avenue and 4th Avenue. The upper blocks are surveyed 25 foot lots with few buildings: scattered frame dwellings, coops and sheds. Below 5th Avenue the New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad crosses the part diagonally; beside it stand the Hawthorne Varnish Works and the J. Dickens sheet metal works, and a feed storage building on Florence Avenue. South of the railroad, along Ethel and 4th Avenues, are dwellings, a woodworking shop and garages, and the trolley right of way is marked at the lower left corner. The large blank area at the top, with the title, the north arrow and lot 4, lies beyond the built-up grid. Six inch water pipes are drawn in several streets. Sheet numbers 173, 195, 196, 197 and 198 mark the adjoining sheets.
notes: Railroad Avenue is Utter Avenue today.
Turned sheet: north is to the left; the part is divided from part 2 by a heavy vertical line.
The trolley right of way at the lower left is followed by today's 4th Avenue north of Van Winkle Avenue.
Copyright stamp dated Aug 28 1922.

map, 100 ft, turned: north to the left; two parts divided by a heavy vertical line: part 1 (left) Van Winkle/Genevieve/Florence/Railroad (Utter) Avs x 4th-9th Avs and Ethel Av; part 2 (right) Lafayette, 1st-4th Avs, Brookview Av, Vreeland Av, Central Av, Goffle Rd, Wagaraw Brook.

sheet-199-2.description: The right part of sheet 199, an additional sheet of April 1922 at 100 feet to an inch, separated from the left part by a heavy vertical line and drawn turned so that north points to the left. It covers the area of Hawthorne south of Rea Avenue along Vreeland Avenue: Lafayette Avenue, 3rd, 2nd and 1st Avenues and Brookview Avenue run across the part from the dividing line to Vreeland Avenue, and Goffle Road crosses the lower part diagonally. 4th Avenue and a strip of the rail yard belonging to sheet 196 appear at the top. The blocks between the dividing line and Vreeland Avenue are surveyed into narrow house lots with rounded corners and only a few dwellings, mostly along Lafayette Avenue. East of Vreeland Avenue a large open tract (lot 24) reaches to Central Avenue, Arlington Avenue and Buena Vista Avenue, which are lettered at the right edge with a few houses facing them. Wagaraw Brook crosses the part from the dividing line to the right edge below Brookview Avenue. Along Goffle Road, at the foot of the part, are dwellings, a barn, a store and storage buildings; the bottom edge is marked no exposure. A twelve inch water pipe runs in Lafayette Avenue and six inch pipes in Goffle Road. Sheet numbers 195, 196, 198, 200 and 201 mark the adjoining sheets, and an arrow points to sheet 200.
notes: Brookview Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap.
Arlington and Buena Vista Avenues reach Vreeland Avenue today; on the sheet they stop at the open tract east of it.
Turned sheet: north is to the left.

map, 100 ft, turned: north to the left; two parts divided by a heavy vertical line: part 1 (left) Van Winkle/Genevieve/Florence/Railroad (Utter) Avs x 4th-9th Avs and Ethel Av; part 2 (right) Lafayette, 1st-4th Avs, Brookview Av, Vreeland Av, Central Av, Goffle Rd, Wagaraw Brook.

sheet-200.description: Sheet 200, an additional sheet of April 1922 at 100 feet to an inch, drawn turned so that north points to the left. It covers the south-western corner of Hawthorne between Arlington Avenue at the top and Goffel Road near the bottom, with Diamond Bridge Avenue along the right edge. Warburton, McKinley and Warren Avenues run down from Arlington Avenue and cross Buena Vista Avenue; Parmelee, Bamford and Howth Avenues run from Warren Avenue to Diamond Bridge Avenue, and May St. is lettered where it leaves to the right. These blocks are laid out in 25 to 50 foot house lots with rows of frame dwellings and garages, densest along Arlington, Buena Vista and Parmelee Avenues. The whole left and middle of the sheet is a large open tract (lot 4) crossed by Wagaraw Brook, which flows under a steel bridge at Diamond Bridge Avenue. Between the brook and Goffel Road stand the cow barns and bottling house of the Shady Brook Dairy. Along Goffel Road, which crosses the sheet diagonally, are dwellings, a wagon house, a stone store, a workshop and coops, and below it a cemetery; the bottom edge is marked no exposure. Six inch water pipes are drawn in most streets and twelve inch pipes in Diamond Bridge Avenue. Sheet numbers 194, 199 and 201 mark the adjoining sheets.
notes: Goffel Road is Goffle Road today; Parmelee Avenue is Parmalee Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Howth Avenue is Brookside Avenue today.
Parmalee, Bamford and Brookside Avenues now continue west of Warren Avenue to McKinley and Warburton Avenues; in 1922 that land was an open tract, so those modern junctions were excluded.
Turned sheet: north is to the left.
Copyright stamp dated Aug 28 1922.

map, 100 ft, turned: north to the left. Arlington, Buena Vista, Warburton, McKinley, Warren, Parmelee (Parmalee), Bamford, Howth (now Brookside Av), Diamond Bridge Avs, Goffel (Goffle) Rd, Wagaraw Brook, cemetery. Parmalee/Bamford west of Warren not built in 1922 (modern junctions excluded). One part.

sheet-201.description: Sheet 201, an additional sheet of April 1922 at 100 feet to an inch, covering central Hawthorne from Central Avenue at the top to Diamond Bridge Avenue at the bottom. The New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad runs straight down the middle between Grand Avenue and Royal Avenue, with a railroad station at Diamond Bridge Avenue. West of the tracks Arlington and Lafayette Avenues are crossed by Warburton, McKinley and Warren Avenues and 1st Street; here stand the Hawthorne M.E. Church, the Hawthorne Public School, an auto service station, the Gideon Silk Company and blocks of frame dwellings. East of the tracks Royal, Forest and Park Avenues are crossed by 3rd, 2nd and Ashley Streets; a broad silk mill with the Hermas Machine Company's machine shop fills much of the block between 3rd and 2nd Streets, and the Excello Hosiery Company stands on Forest Avenue near Diamond Bridge Avenue. The right side of the sheet is a newer tract laid out on the skew, with Frederick, Franklin, Virginia, Kingston, Post and Van Winkle Avenues running diagonally across narrow, mostly empty house lots, and Washington and Hawthorne Avenues below them at the lower right. 5th Av. enters at the top at Park Avenue. Six, eight and twelve inch water pipes are drawn in the streets, and the right edge is marked no exposure. Sheet numbers 194, 198, 199, 200 and 202 mark the adjoining sheets.
notes: 2nd Street is Warburton Avenue today; Ashley Street is Ashley Place.
The unnamed 40 ft street between Lafayette and Grand Avenues north of the school is Legion Place today; 1st Street between them is not in OpenStreetMap.
The diagonal tract (Frederick to Van Winkle Avenues) was not used as control: its streets could not be matched to modern ones with confidence.
Copyright stamp dated Aug 28 1922.

map, 100 ft. Arlington, Lafayette, Grand, Royal, Forest, Park Avs, Central Av, Warburton, McKinley, Warren Avs, 1st, 2nd (now Warburton Av), 3rd, Ashley Sts, Diamond Bridge Av, diagonal tract of Frederick, Franklin, Virginia, Kingston, Post, Van Winkle Avs (not used), Washington, Hawthorne Avs; NYS&W RR. One part.

sheet-202.description: Sheet 202, an additional sheet of April 1922 at 100 feet to an inch, covering the south-eastern part of Hawthorne from Diamond Bridge Avenue at the top down to Wagaraw Road, between the New York, Susquehanna and Western Railroad on the left edge and the Bergen County line on the right. The Erie Railroad crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the upper right. Royal Avenue runs down beside the Susquehanna tracks, and Washington and Charles run down the middle on a slant, crossed by Division, Midland and Cross; Wagner and Park are lettered at the top. St. Anthony's R.C. Church with its rectory and sisters' house stands at Diamond Bridge Avenue, and a mirror manufacturer's building on Washington. The blocks between Washington and Charles are long narrow lots, mostly empty. South-east of the Erie, Passaic, Lincoln and Bergen Avenues run down to Wagaraw Road, crossed by Loretto and Columbus Avenues; these blocks are closely built with frame dwellings, stores, a copper smith and Hawthorne Public School No. 2. The borough line between Hawthorne and Bergen County is drawn as a dash-dot line down Lincoln Avenue. In the lower left corner, at Wagaraw Road, are the Hawthorne Chemical Company's tanning extract works and coal pockets, and Ethel, Vincent and Schoon frame a small block with a workshop and the ruins of a fire. Six and eight inch water pipes are drawn in the streets. Sheet numbers 172, 194 and 201 mark the adjoining sheets.
notes: Charles is Hawthorne Avenue today; Division is Division Street, Wagner is Wagner Place, Midland is Midland Avenue, Vincent is Vincent Street and Schoon is Schoon Avenue.
Bergen Avenue was not matched to a modern street and was not used as control; Cross is not in OpenStreetMap (possibly Harrison Place).
Junctions of Midland and Wagner and of Diamond Bridge and Royal Avenues were left out: the detector paired a street edge with another line there.
Copyright stamp dated Aug 28 1922.

map, 100 ft. Diamond Bridge, Royal, Washington, Charles (now Hawthorne Av), Division, Wagner, Midland, Park, Cross, Ethel, Vincent, Schoon, Passaic, Loretto, Lincoln, Bergen, Columbus Avs, Wagaraw Rd; Erie RR diagonal; Hawthorne/Bergen County line in Lincoln Av. One part.
